title: Stock cover in weeks
summary: Turn stock on hand and weekly sales into weeks of cover, then label each style Low, OK or Overstock.

blocks.text: A pile of 300 pairs can be too much or too little. It depends on how fast the style sells. Stock cover answers it: how many weeks will today's stock last at the current rate of sales?
You will calculate cover for six styles, handle a style that has stopped selling, and label every style Low, OK, Overstock or Check.

items: Objective: calculate stock cover with a zero-sales guard and label it against low and overstock limits.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: Stock cover in weeks = stock on hand (B2) divided by average weekly sales (C2). 120 pairs at 40 pairs a week is 3 weeks of cover.
If a style sold nothing, C2 is 0 and the division fails with #DIV/0!. A style with no sales has no meaningful cover, so show a clear message instead of an error.
ROUND keeps 1 decimal place. IFERROR replaces the error with the text No sales. Text results need double quotes.
Nested IF tests one rule at a time. First the no-sales case, then below the low limit, then above the overstock limit. Anything left is OK. The limits sit in G2 and G3, locked with $ signs.
Tip: check the special case (No sales) first. Comparing the text No sales with a number would give a wrong answer if you tested the limits first.
Four questions on stock cover. Type numbers without commas, for example 8.

items: Stock cover (weeks) = stock on hand / average weekly sales.
IFERROR guards the division when weekly sales are 0.
ROUND(x,1) keeps one decimal place so the numbers are easy to read.
A nested IF labels the cover against limits kept in cells, testing the special case first.

blocks.text: Next: reorder quantity, to turn cover targets into an order.

items.prompt: A style has 240 pairs on hand and sells 30 pairs a week. How many weeks of cover is that?
A style has 95 pairs on hand and sells 40 a week. What does =ROUND(95/40,1) return?
Why use IFERROR(ROUND(B2/C2,1),"No sales") instead of the plain division?

options.label: When weekly sales are 0 the division gives #DIV/0!, and IFERROR turns that into a readable message
Because it makes the cover number larger
Because it stops stock on hand going negative

items.prompt: A style sells twice as fast as before, and stock on hand stays the same. What happens to its cover in weeks?
